title: Builds, unit tests, and Git — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: A team makes the expense tracker reproducible. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: To use a declared Maven version reproducibly

questions.explanation: The wrapper bootstraps the specified build tool.

questions.prompt: What should a unit test usually assert?

options.text: The exact number of local variables

questions.explanation: Behavior assertions survive safe internal refactoring.

questions.prompt: Which dependency scope fits JUnit in a Maven application?
questions.explanation: Test dependencies need not become production runtime dependencies.

questions.prompt: What is a useful parameterized test?

options.text: A test that uses random sleep
A test for every getter regardless of behavior
One behavior exercised with several meaningful inputs

questions.explanation: Tables of cases express boundaries and variations clearly.

questions.prompt: What should be reviewed before committing?

options.text: The staged diff and relevant test results

questions.explanation: Review the exact changes and their validation.

questions.prompt: Which dependency makes an expiry test nondeterministic unless controlled?
questions.explanation: Injecting Clock makes time-based behavior predictable.
1000 and 20 satisfy the domain bounds. The discount is 200, leaving 800. A percentage of 101 must be rejected rather than creating a negative price.
